newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market quiet in thin demand.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market quiet in thin demand.

text.p: Vietnam's rice prices continued a gradual downwards slide over the past week, tracking the recent fall in the value of the domestic currency against the dollar.
Dealers quoted five percent broken grade in quiet trade on Thursday at around $263 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, slightly lower than last week's $263-$265 level.
Ten percent broken was quoted at around $253-$258 per tonne.
They said ten vessels were in Saigon port at present, but some were believed to be shipments delayed by congestion. Details of destinations were not available.
Vietnam's currency, the dong, has fallen in value by around four percent in recent weeks following moves by the central bank to engineer a more competitive rate for local exports.

Harvesting of the spring-winter crop in the Mekong Delta began earlier this month. The government says it is hoping that 1997 exports will exceed last year's total of just over three million tonnes. ($1 = 11,650 dong)
